problem: g518 retained 1468.149ms waiting for the local service ACK while its matching native apply measured 151.812ms. The six inner native-child spans and three parent spans do not cover the outer journal response boundary.
observation: g520 ackRead.serviceIPC records the outer same-host exchange only after matching sequence/op. Six disjoint durations use the existing native IPC shape: phase 0 is zero, then request submission to journal read, read through handling to reply-ready, reply-ready through write admission, native WriteFile submission point to app first positive Read return, then remaining decode. No raw timestamp is exported.
wire: Existing profiled local ACK suffix expands 44 -> 68 bytes, reserving 24 bytes for three outer QPC stamps beside the normalized inner profile. Both matching installed images are updated together. No new input, request, round trip or read/write operation. Peer network protocol is unchanged.
coexistence: Outer stamps do not replace native-child apply/submission or parent timing. Absent/invalid optional metadata is not an input result. Failed/truncated/foreign ACKs cannot publish a confirmed outer service profile.
nativeSubmission: serviceNativeWrite=true means pinned ACK bytes were stamped after the native pipe write mutex/event/pinning and immediately before WriteFile. Offset validation precedes I/O; the deadline is rechecked after the clock call. False means the io.Writer fallback, not a native submission observation. Flags/timestamps are patched only before submission and never reused after a failed write.
limits: Reply-ready, pre-WriteFile submission and app read return are observations, not kernel arrival or Write completion. Scheduling can still occur between a timestamp and its following instruction. Phase 4 includes transfer and app resumption and cannot by itself prove either cause. Outer spans contain input work and overlap inner native timing; never add them. The request-to-read span includes app Write, so the service profile is not bounded by ClientResponse alone.
budget: The existing tracked-input probe/window budget applies. QPC order and total <=120s are validated; unavailable clocks drop timing. Deep-copy ownership prevents caller mutation after collection. Input order, authority, outcomes and deadlines are unchanged.
validation: Tests cover outer/inner coexistence, absent inner detail, reserved bytes, following-ACK framing, production serve population, matching-ACK/presence/window validation and snapshot ownership. A real-QPC transport test separates 12ms service processing from 18ms app read resumption. Actual Windows pipe tests hold the writer gate for 20ms and verify native submission happens afterward, and reject invalid/expired writes without claiming submission. Full related packages, vet and selected race tests run before rollout.
rolloutRefinement: g519 was packaged but not installed. g520 includes the more precise native write-admission boundary and retains the same 68-byte suffix. The installed comparison baseline remains g518 on both PCs.
delivery: Physical results and paired installation are recorded separately. No current root-cause resolution or measured physical improvement is claimed. No external API, DB, runner or repository hygiene change.
